correctness.rationale: For integer boxes the maximum coordinate difference bounds every greatest common divisor by the longest side \(L\), with equality only when all coordinate differences are integral multiples of \(L\). This forces every shorter coordinate to agree and every longest coordinate difference to be \(0\) or \(\pm L\). Freezing short and interior coordinates gives exactly \(B\binom{k}{s}(L-1)^{k-s}\) disjoint complete components of order \(2^s\). Edge counting, unique diameter lines, colorings, direction counts and the exact polynomial follow by binomial identities. Unimodular maps preserve gcd and the lattice. The independent all-pairs program passed 207 finite instances, corroborating but not proving the general statement.

value.rationale: Lattice diameter segments form a natural Ehrhart-like geometric counting invariant, and integral parallelepipeds are their canonical high-dimensional test class. The exact finite graph and full counting/coloring polynomials strengthen the published existence-only eventual quasipolynomial statement to an explicit polynomial of degree \(d-1\), period one, valid for every positive integer dilation. The optimal lattice Borsuk number changes sharply with the number of longest lattice-edge directions, and full clique-size multiplicities quantify that transition.
